Read an area of interest

Source: R/aoi.R
read_aoi.Rd

Reads an area of interest (AOI) from polygons, a file or bounds, and returns it as an sf polygon layer, optionally reprojected and dissolved into one feature. It is the one entry point for AOIs in constechr, so every tool reads an AOI the same way before rasterizing or extracting data for it.

Usage

read_aoi(x, crs = NULL, union = TRUE)

Arguments

x

The AOI, one of:

  • an sf data frame or sfc geometry column of polygons or multipolygons;

  • a terra SpatVector of polygons;

  • a file path (a single string) to a vector file that GDAL can read, such as a shapefile (.shp), GeoPackage (.gpkg) or GeoJSON (.geojson). For a file or folder with more than one layer, such as a file geodatabase, name the layer as <path>/<layer>, for example "data.gdb/aoi";

  • bounds: a numeric vector c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) (named, in any order, or unnamed in that order), an sf bbox (from sf::st_bbox()) or a terra SpatExtent.

crs

The target coordinate reference system (CRS): anything sf::st_crs() accepts, such as an EPSG code (3347), a WKT or "EPSG:<code>" string, a crs object, or a spatial object (sf, SpatRaster, SpatVector) whose CRS to use. NULL (the default) keeps the input's CRS. For bounds that carry no CRS (a numeric vector or a SpatExtent), crs is required and is the CRS the bounds are in.

union

A single logical. TRUE (the default) dissolves all the polygons into one feature and drops their attributes; FALSE keeps the features and their attributes as they are.

Value

An sf data frame of POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON geometries in the target CRS (the input's when crs is NULL), with its geometry column named geometry. With union = TRUE, one row and no attribute columns; with union = FALSE, one row per input feature with its attributes. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Reading: files are read with sf::st_read() (GDAL), from the layer named in the path, or from the file's only layer.

  • Bounds: become one rectangle with its corners at the bounds (sf::st_as_sfc() of an sf::st_bbox()).

  • Geometry: Z and M coordinates are dropped (sf::st_zm()), so the AOI is two-dimensional. Geometries are neither validated nor repaired.

  • CRS: when crs differs from the input's CRS, the AOI is reprojected with sf::st_transform() (PROJ), which moves each vertex; edges are not densified, so a rectangle keeps its four corners. When crs is NULL or the same as the input's, coordinates are left untouched.

  • Dissolve (union = TRUE): sf::st_union(), after reprojection, in the target CRS. In a projected CRS the union is planar (GEOS). In a geographic (longitude and latitude) CRS it is spherical (s2) when sf::sf_use_s2() is TRUE, sf's default, and planar otherwise.

  • No areas or lengths are computed.

See also

Other aoi: rasterize_aoi()

Examples

# From a file: the example AOI, a GeoPackage with one layer
path <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
aoi <- read_aoi(path)
aoi
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...

# Naming the layer, and reprojecting to longitude and latitude
read_aoi(file.path(path, "aoi"), crs = 4326)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -83.44661 ymin: 44.69229 xmax: -83.41441 ymax: 44.71665
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((-83.44661 44.6960...

# In the CRS of a template raster
template <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
)
read_aoi(path, crs = template)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003600 ymin: 604300 xmax: 1005800 ymax: 606600
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003600 606600, 1...

# From bounds, which need a CRS
read_aoi(
  c(xmin = 1003000, ymin = 604000, xmax = 1006000, ymax = 607000),
  crs = template
)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 0 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>                         geometry
#> 1 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
